questions.question: On a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel tired.
Dress warmly to stay protected from cold wind and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to stay protected from cold wind and rain.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue. Ride no more than 6 hours per day. Take a rest break at least every 2 hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants, as you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: How can you stop other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: Make angry facial expressions at them.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to leave no large space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back without making the new rider lead.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can reduce your ability to ride safely. Riding a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way is to change lanes and let them pass if it is safe to do so. Speeding up may make them follow faster and increase danger.

questions.question: What should you use your mirrors for when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To check if parked cars are entering the road.
To see if vehicles are changing lanes.
To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
To see if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors to check for cars coming up behind you. Drivers may not see you until they are very close, so you may need to react quickly.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because it will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When you adjust your mirrors, what should you see?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. You may see the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: How do you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Swerve back and forth in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to prevent other drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders ride in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the new rider lead the group.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: Slower than you would during the day under similar conditions.
At the same speed as during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under similar conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, go slower than you would during the day with similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally used, riders should switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: A wobble, or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars, may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans in a curve, the tires have less grip than when the motorcycle is upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When riding at night, how should your following distance compare to daytime riding?

options.text: You should stay farther behind the vehicle ahead of you at night.
You should stay closer behind the vehicle ahead of you at night.
You should always keep the same following distance day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should stay farther behind the vehicle ahead of you at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distance because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. You should stay farther back from the vehicle ahead when riding at night than during the day.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while seated.
Has a seat even with your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits properly if you can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on the seat. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Which of the following best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection in South Carolina. All riders should wear helmets for safety. Passengers should wear fitted clothing so nothing catches on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator during turns. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your body removes about one alcoholic drink per hour. A person drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours. How many drinks are likely still in their system 3 hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. This person had 7 drinks. In 3 hours after their last drink, the body removes 3 drinks. This leaves 4 drinks in their system.

questions.question: When securing a load on a motorcycle, where should you place it?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible. High loads raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and make it harder to balance. Distribute the load evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: Alternate between low and high beams

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams in foggy conditions or near other vehicles.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: Slowing down by turning the engine off
Not encouraged because it damages the engine

questions.explanation: Engine braking is shifting to a lower gear to slow down. It works like applying the brakes.
